10 Hacks Every watchOS 27 User Should Know

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1353 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, watchOS 27 introduces a solid set of upgrades to your wrist—assuming your Apple Watch supports it.
  • With watchOS 27, Apple changed what double-pressing the Digital Crown does.
  • It seems Apple realized the mistake, however, as evidenced by watchOS 27.2.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, watchOS 27 introduces a solid set of upgrades to your wrist—assuming your Apple Watch supports it. While the newest update isn't Apple's most feature-filled, it does include a number of changes that improve the way you exercise, track your health, and locate missing items. That's especially true for anyone with the latest Series 12 or Ultra 4. If your Apple Watch supports watchOS 27, you should know about these 10 hacks:.

With watchOS 27, Apple changed what double-pressing the Digital Crown does. Instead of opening the app switcher, it now triggers Audio Intelligence—if you have an Apple Watch Series 12 or Ultra 4. If you don't have access to those features, the gesture now does nothing.

It seems Apple realized the mistake, however, as evidenced by watchOS 27.2. When you're using an app while running this latest upgrade, press and hold the bottom part of the watch's screen, and you'll trigger the app switcher. You can now jump to a different app, or close an app that isn't working. Sadly, this only works when you're already in an app, and not when you're on the Home Screen, but it's certainly better than nothing.

While you can load up multiple complications on your Apple Watch, they aren't exactly dynamic. That's why I'm a massive fan of the Smart Stack widgets on the Apple Watch, which update dynamically to show contextual information. Now, with the latest Siri Modular Face, you can access dynamic widgets on the Home Screen. If you've just parked your car, for example, you'll see a widget showing its location; likewise, if you have an upcoming calendar appointment, it will be front and center.

It has been revealed that to use the Siri Modular watch face, tap and hold on the screen, go to the end of the list, tap the Plus button, and find and add the Siri Modular watch face. Once you do, you'll start seeing dynamic widgets when you wake up your watch. Don't expect much personalization from this watch face, however. You can customize the colors and add three small complications, but that's it.

Sources indicate that the double-tap gesture is one of my favorite Apple Watch features. By tapping your thumb and index finger together twice, you can do things like answer a call or reply to a message. In watchOS 27, Apple took the gesture one step forward. You can now use the double-tap gesture to scroll through your widgets; if you perform a single tap, it then opens the highlighted widget or the shortcut. This means you can open and browse the weather app, or start a workout, without ever touching your Apple Watch's screen.

Recent findings suggest that your Apple Watch's newly introduced Music Recognition app has native Shazam integration. What's more, Shazam will record your request even when you're offline and away from your iPhone. The moment you reconnect, the service will identify the songs, which you can see in the Shazam app on your iPhone or Apple Watch.

It seems like Apple has a library of songs it uses for offline recognition, because in my testing, it was able to recognize a Coldplay song instantly, even when in Airplane mode. To use it, you can either open the Music Recognition app, or you can add the widget for faster access. Scroll up on the Home Screen, go to the bottom of the screen, tap the Edit button, then the Plus button, and add the Music Recognition widget.

Apple Watches have traditionally lacked a live step count widget or complication. To find your step count, you had to go to the bottom of the Activity app, or rely on third-party apps. But even still, these apps never highlighted live data. You’d always have to wait a couple of seconds to see the updated stats.

Now, if you own the latest Apple Watch Series 12 or the Ultra 4, you can add a live step count widget or complication to the Apple Watch face or the Smart Stack. This will show you your precise step count at all times. To use it, go to the bottom of the Smart Stack, tap the Edit button, then tap the Plus button. Here, find and add the newly introduced Step count widget.

Siri is no longer a voice assistant that you use for one-off tasks. With Siri AI, you can now carry on multiple conversations with context and memory. It's not as robust as ChatGPT or Claude, but you can use Siri AI for brainstorming, researching, and jotting down ideas for later.

Recent findings suggest that the Siri AI app on the iPhone shows all your conversations, and so does the Apple Watch. This means you can continue your Siri AI conversations and view past chats on your Apple Watch. To use it, press the Digital Crown once, then tap the Siri app icon in the center. This will open up all your conversations instead of calling upon Siri. Tap a conversation to continue your chat on the Apple Watch. Of course, anything you do here will be reflected in the Siri app on your iPhone.

Industry observers note that the new Find My app on the Apple Watch reveals a single map for finding people, devices, and items. This means you can now locate your family members who are sharing their location with you, as well as AirTags or other Find My items from the watchOS app.

After opening the app, you can use the Digital Crown to zoom in or out of the map. Use touch to pan around. The map doesn't show all items and people at once, though. Tap the Menu button at the bottom-right corner, and then switch between People, Items, or Devices. If you have multiple items, you can scroll through them using the Digital Crown.

It has been revealed that while it's not a Whoop-level feature, the Apple Watch now includes a Readiness score. Instead of individually looking at your training load, sleep score, and vitals, you now have one number that gives you the whole picture.

The Readiness score ranges from 0 to 10 and is based on your recent fitness activity, sleep data, and background health monitoring. If you have a score of 8 to 10, your Apple Watch thinks you can push yourself, or "go for it," as it states; if it's below 5, the watch thinks you should consider lighter activity. This feature, though, is only available on Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4. You can use the upcoming Readiness app on your Apple Watch to see this data, but you can also access it on your iPhone in the Fitness app's new Readiness section.

Low Power Mode isn't your only option when it comes to extending the battery life for your Apple Watch. watchOS 27 offers a special Max Extended Workout mode just for long workouts. With it, your Apple Watch disables some features, like splits and alerts, and reduces the frequency of GPS and heart rate readings, in the hopes of extending your battery throughout your entire exercise. To use it, go to the Workout app and select the workout you want. Tap the Goals button in the top-right corner, and choose the Extended option. Then, switch to the Max Extended option and start your workout.

According to recent reports, the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 come with a set of Audio Intelligence features that use the microphones on the Apple Watch, paired with AI models (both local and cloud-based), to identify sounds, music, and record conversation. Thanks to this new feature, one of the iPhone's accessibility features also makes its way to the Apple Watch.

According to recent reports, sound Recognition can alert you when it hears sirens, alarms, doorbells, and more, even when your iPhone isn’t around. To set this up, go to the Settings app on your iPhone and navigate to Accessibility > Sound & Name Recognition > Sound Recognition. Here, enable the sounds you want to monitor, and make sure to turn on the Detect using Apple Watch toggle.

According to recent reports, somehow, Cyberleek, the notorious hacker behind multiple Grand Theft Auto 6 leaks, has returned. "It is done. CL holds the full November 2026 build of Grand Theft Auto 6, and it is going out by torrent," a statement from Cyberleek reads (via Kotaku). "Now. However, there's no guarantee the game can be emulated, and Cyberleek added that they'll "work to get a PS5 build" if people keep supporting them. This isn't the first time Cyberleek has threatened to release a pirated build of GTA 6; back in October, they promised to do so if their meme coin reached $30 million in value. While Cyberleek initially claimed to act in gamers' interests when they first burst onto the scene, they true motives were quickly revealed when they started hyping up their meme coin--reportedly part of a pump-and-dump scheme. While Cyberleek has yet to be identified, their actions did lead to GTA 6 developer Rockstar Games to issue a statement, in which it described the leaks as "heartbreaking" after years of work on the game. ⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, AI safety for both adults and children is under greater scrutiny than ever before, with a growing number of questions and concerns appearing around how beneficial or otherwise these conversational bots actually are for our mental well-being—even without considering their energy use, ethics, or economic implications.
  • The significant AI apps, such as ChatGPT and Gemini, are right in the center of these trends, and the companies behind them are taking steps that they promise will keep children safe.
  • Recent findings suggest that openAI's ChatGPT has one of the more comprehensive setups in terms of parental controls.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, AI safety for both adults and children is under greater scrutiny than ever before, with a growing number of questions and concerns appearing around how beneficial or otherwise these conversational bots actually are for our mental well-being—even without considering their energy use, ethics, or economic implications. At the same time, an increasing number of apps and services are becoming age-gated in a growing number of countries around the world, as governments realize that letting kids loose on AI apps, social media platforms, and the web at large might not be the best idea for their ongoing development and prosperity.

The significant AI apps, such as ChatGPT and Gemini, are right in the center of these trends, and the companies behind them are taking steps that they promise will keep children safe. If you want to know what youngsters in your family may be getting exposed to, and what you can do about it, here's the rundown.

Recent findings suggest that openAI's ChatGPT has one of the more comprehensive setups in terms of parental controls. The minimum age for users is 13, and if you're under 18, you need to have parental consent to open an account—age is predicted via several signals, including what times of day you use ChatGPT and what you talk about.

Industry observers note that accounts for under-18s automatically become ChatGPT for Teens accounts. There's more of a focus on learning and study (with a dedicated study mode), as well as "age-appropriate safeguards to help reduce exposure to sensitive or potentially harmful content." There are built-in protections for "harmful topics," including sexual, romantic, or violent roleplay, graphic violence, and self-harm. These work on top of the safeguards for all owners that limit chats about physical harm and illegal activity.

These ChatGPT for Teens accounts can also be linked to a parental account—but while parental consent is required for under-18s to use the service, ChatGPT clearly states that teens do have the option to break the link if they want. If you do persuade your kid to keep your accounts connected, you can set time limits on when the AI bot can be used, and tweak some of the sensitivity settings. However, you can't view any conversations.

To set up parental controls from ChatGPT on the web, click your profile icon (bottom left), then Settings > Parental controls > Add family member and follow the instructions. It's also worth bearing in mind that ChatGPT app can also be used for free, anonymously, in any web browser, though OpenAI notes people accessing the AI this way are subject to the default under-18s limits (and can't save chats or access an archive).

In a recent development, gemini is tied into everything else Google does, and follows the broader rules for Google accounts: No under-13s, unless you're part of a family group and using an account managed by an adult. You can manage your family through the Family Link portal on the web, though as far as parental controls specific to Gemini go, you can only enable or disable access to the AI (settings like screen time apply across all enabled apps).

Industry observers note that for all under-18s (partly identified through age estimation), whether or not they're part of a managed family group, Google applies some additional protections. They include preventing the AI from taking on a persona, guarding against emotional dependence on the AI, and discouraging bullying and other forms of harassment. There are also safeguards to limit chats about age-restricted substances like alcohol or vapes, and mental health problems like eating disorders.

Industry observers note that these protections for minors are applied in addition to the usual guardrails in Gemini for everyone. The guardrails should lead you away from conversations about self-harm, suicide, violence, and illegal activities, and offer quick links to support in times of crisis. However, Google itself admits that these filters aren't perfect.

As with ChatGPT, there's a loophole of sorts in that anyone can start chatting with Gemini, for free inside a web browser, with no checks at all. These conversations can't be saved and come up against usage limits fairly quickly, but they're only protected by the general restrictions for all accounts, not the ones specific to minors.

In a recent development, meta AI will show up in several apps that young people and children are likely to use, including WhatsApp and Instagram, as well as having its own separate app on the web and on phones. The standard restrictions for Meta's social media accounts apply to its AI too: A minimum age of 13, and restrictions for all under-18s. Like many other platforms, it uses some AI magic to flag up accounts being used by minors.

According to recent reports, if you're under 18 and on a Meta Teen account, you'll come up against blocks if you try to get Meta AI to engage in sexual or romantic roleplay, or discuss alcohol or substance misuse. Chats on topics such as eating disorders and self-harm will prompt the AI to offer guidance towards relevant support services.

Meta offers a comprehensive parental control setup for its apps, including Meta AI, but connecting a parent account isn't compulsory for teens. This is handled through the Meta Family Center portal, and parents can get reports on the general topics that kids are chatting about with AI—though they don't get the exact transcripts or prompts. Any self-harm or suicide discussion can trigger an alert to the connected parent account.

All consumers, under 18 or over 18, get support and crisis intervention responses when chatting about suicide and self-harm, and there are strict limits on discussing illegal and harmful acts, including drug use and cyberbullying, as well as sexual and adult content.

Apple owners have to be 13 or over to have an account, which is required to access Siri AI—anyone younger needs to have an account created for them by an adult, and these accounts can only get at the basic, older Siri. Date of birth must be declared when opening an Apple account, with tighter checks rolling out in many parts of the world.

According to recent reports, anyone over the age of 13 can have an Apple account and use the Siri AI app, with or without a connected parent account, as it stands in most U.S. states. This means the well-being safeguards are essentially the same for teens as they are for adults: There are safeguards around self-harm, suicide, sexual and violent content, and illegal commands. It's one of the more conservative AIs when it comes to what it will talk about.

Recent findings suggest that the new and improved Siri AI can be managed to some extent by the new parental controls available in iOS 27 and Apple's other software updates for 2026—Apple has clearly seen the way the wind is blowing—but this is optional for teens. It depends on whether or not you can corral your kids into a Family Sharing group.

If your teens are in your family group of users, then the standard Screen Time rules apply for controlling app usage limits and device access (in iOS Settings, tap your name, then Family to get at them). There are also options for disabling certain Siri AI features, such as the writing tools or the image creation capabilities.

Industry observers note that like Gemini/Google and Apple/Siri, Copilot is tied into the wider Microsoft ecosystem, and access for under-18s can be managed through it. Consumers must be 13 or older to hold a Microsoft or a Copilot account—and again, there's some underlying tech in place to detect anyone who might be deliberately lying about their age.

If you've got a teen using Copilot, you can manage their access through the standard Microsoft Family Safety portal. You're able to enable or disable Copilot access, set times during which Copilot can and can't be used, and disable certain features like image generation or voice mode. Parents can't read the Copilot chats of their kids, though.

Industry observers note that parental supervision is optional—a teen aged 13–17 can use Copilot without linking their account to an adult one. Microsoft notes users identified as under 18 won't see personalized results or ads, and will get age-appropriate responses regarding risky or harmful content, though there's not much detail on what that entails.

More generally, content around self-harm, violence, adult content, harassment, and harmful or illegal activity is banned on the AI platform. Any prompts about suicide or drugs will bring up support options rather than answers, whether you're an adult or a young person using the service.

Ultimately that means that minors have the same access to Grok as adults, if they want it—an AI platform that combines "weak safety guardrails" and "a range of extremely harmful content" that includes "explicit sexual content, mental health risks, violent content, and inappropriate responses to... offensive content" (that's the Common Sense Media Report again).

In a recent development, yes, this is the AI chatbot that has previously had a problem with deepfake porn imagery, and which has traditionally taken a rather casual attitude towards safety concerns, led by SpaceXAI CEO Elon Musk. While illegal and harmful content is supposedly banned from Grok, its own FAQs admit that certain chats can result in "dialogue that may involve coarse language, crude humor, sexual situations, or violence.".

There is actually a Grok Kids Mode that limits the kind of content that can be shown and the conversation topics that can be added, but it requires users to self-declare themselves as minors and is easy to bypass. The advice from Common Sense Media seems to be the way to go with Grok: Do not let your teens access it.

In a recent development, claude's approach to child safety is straightforward: You can only register for an account if you're over 18. It is possible to lie about your age when signing up, but like the other platforms, Anthropic looks at various "signals" in behavior to spot minors—if your account gets flagged, you have to verify your age using an option like face age estimation or Yoti.

There's no free web access to the chatbot, like there is with ChatGPT and Gemini, so if you're under 18, you're locked out from the service unless you know the behavioral tricks to get past Claude's detection systems.

In terms of more general well-being protections on Claude, any chat around self-harm or suicide will guide users towards helplines and other resources for support. Conversations about illegal activities, disallowed speech, and explicit sexual content are banned from the platform. In recent months, Anthropic indicates it's also reduced AI sycophancy.

That's something of a whistle-stop tour of the major seven AI chatbots, but if you're a parent, it should give you some idea of what's out there and how easy it is to access. Besides the parental controls built into these AIs (or not), you also have the settings available at the platform level—Android, iOS, Windows, macOS—to restrict the use of any potentially harmful apps.

The day after the midterm elections, President Donald Trump met with Susie Wiles in the Oval Office. He asked his chief of staff whether she believed Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth would survive the impeachment attempt that would soon be introduced by a member of his own party.

Hegseth was in a precarious position. He had been among the most aggressive champions of the war with Iran, widely seen as the policy most responsible for the shellacking Republicans had taken the night before. Wiles remained officially supportive of Hegseth throughout her time in the White House, but she had harbored concerns about the secretary from the start. She did not believe he was forthright about his skeletons during a rocky confirmation process, and she considered the subsequent Signalgate scandal an amateurish disaster.

Sources indicate that in the Wednesday meeting, according to a senior White House official, Wiles made clear that the war, the uncertainty of its next steps, and the inflation it had fueled all contributed to the midterms debacle. She offered her resignation, but Trump declined. On Thursday night, in a contentious meeting in the Oval Office, she offered to resign again. Trump announced the next day that Wiles would leave the White House for his outside political operation.

Hegseth’s fate was still uncertain. A deeply unpopular figure among the American public, presiding over an even more unpopular war, he faced an impeachment push led by Representative Thomas Massie. “He is just failing,” stated Republican senator Thom Tillis of North Carolina—who voted to confirm Hegseth at the start of Trump’s term—in an interview with Vanity Fair. “In the same way that Kristi Noem failed at Homeland Security, he simply doesn’t have the instincts or the prior experience as an executive that is necessary for this particular role.”.

According to recent reports, the secretary of defense has now embarked on a campaign to save his job, and Stephen Miller’s elevation to replace Wiles as Trump’s chief of staff has helped to ensure a reprieve. Trump has so far backed Hegseth publicly, and last week, House Republicans blocked the impeachment effort. “Pete is a fighter,” the White House official explained. “Trump likes fighters.” And there are other reasons to keep him in place, the official said: Confirming a replacement will not be easy, particularly when Democrats take control of Congress, and ousting Hegseth would signal an admission that at this point, Trump’s war is a failure.

Industry observers note that it was the president’s taste for staffers out of central casting that helped put Hegseth—a weekend morning television host with no experience in government, but with the square jaw of an Army Wives extra—in charge of the Department of Defense. He has relied on his talents before the cameras, and a team of advisers attuned to the production of his persona, to both keep his job and sell Trump on aggressive military action from the Pacific to the Persian Gulf. His survival has depended in part on his ability to project strength—not to the public, or to the rank-and-file, but to the president.

Recent findings suggest that “In just under two years, Secretary Hegseth has worked side-by-side with President Trump to restore American power on the world stage, build the strongest military in generations, and instill a warrior ethos at the Pentagon,” White House spokeswoman Olivia Wales mentioned in a statement. “President Trump and Secretary Hegseth have taken bold, necessary action to deny the Iranian regime the ability to develop a nuclear weapon, bring narco-terrorist Nicolas Maduro to American justice, and defend our homeland from dangerous terrorists and cartels—saving American lives.”.

“They will stand behind him in the short term,” remarked a second senior administration official. And yet, “He is a cost. He’s constantly requiring people to spend political capital on him. The White House is constantly having to come in and save him. The question is, at what point is it too much of a cost to the president?”.

The morning after Hegseth survived the impeachment attempt, he attended a Veterans Day ceremony at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier. Hegseth was joined at the sacred memorial by his closest aides: Jennifer Hegseth, his third wife and a former Fox News producer who serves as an informal but influential adviser; his chief of staff Ricky Buria, a Marine Corps veteran who followed an unusual path into the top brass; and Tami Radabaugh, another former Fox News producer whom Hegseth hired as a senior adviser.

As the group posed for photos at the Tomb, they chatted and laughed loudly. A US Army sentinel guarding the memorial turned to the group and shouted out a reprimand: “All visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times.” After video of the moment made for embarrassing headlines, Hegseth awarded the soldier a Joint Service Commendation Medal and posed alongside several Army officers for a photoshoot that was posted on his social media accounts. The Pentagon did not elaborate on why a soldier was awarded a medal for an act as pedestrian as scolding noisy attendees at a memorial. “Hegseth would not have given him that award had the incident not been on TV,” said a former senior defense official.

Industry observers note that the small group of advisers beside Hegseth has helped the secretary weather a series of scandals in his two years as defense secretary using stage-managed displays of toughness. “He’s a cross between a carnival barker and a personal trainer,” remarked John Ullyot, who served as chief Pentagon spokesperson and senior adviser to Hegseth until he left the department last year. A loyal Trump backer, Ullyot initially supported Hegseth’s calls to restore standards and excise identity politics from the military. He has since emerged as a fierce public critic and now believes Hegseth should resign.

In his new book, The President Deserves Better, Ullyot describes a secretary of defense fixated on self-promotion and content creation. Jennifer plays an instrumental role in those efforts, directing the secretary’s social media and a small battalion of accounts that support him online. “It was as if she was producing him in his role as Secretary,” Ullyot writes. She has helped produce—and starred in—dramatic videos of Hegseth posted by the Pentagon’s official social media accounts. “Her entire job is to make his image,” one source told Vanity Fair.

House Republican Thomas Massie, who brought the articles of impeachment against Hegseth last week, argued the bombing was “the result of systemic deterioration and removal of Department of Defense infrastructure that Congress had mandated by law to limit collateral damage to civilians.”.

According to recent reports, her role extended well beyond production, alarming senior officials in the Department of Defense. She interviewed candidates for Pentagon roles. She attended sensitive bilateral meetings with foreign officials. She was included in Signal chats that discussed the war plans for the Houthi operation in Yemen. The former defense official stated they warned Hegseth about his wife’s involvement in Pentagon affairs. “She did not have a fucking clearance,” they said. “She shouldn’t be privy to this shit.”.

Recent findings suggest that hegseth himself seemed too smitten to care. He covered the walls of his office, as well as other meeting rooms and corridors throughout the Pentagon, with large photos of himself and his wife. When The New York Times examined Jennifer’s influence at the department over the summer, Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell called the former cable news producer “an accomplished leader.” He added that the Pentagon “not only welcomes her current leadership but actively plans to involve her even more deeply in the future.” Politico later reported that while advising the secretary of defense, Jennifer was being paid for consulting work by Watchtower Strategies, a Washington lobbying shop that counts Lockheed Martin as a client.

Sources indicate that she wasn’t the only Fox News producer at the Pentagon. Hegseth also gave Radabaugh—a former producer on Fox & Friends Weekend with no government experience—broad authority over department affairs, I’m told. Radabaugh made sure that glamorous photos and videos of Hegseth were published online promptly, sometimes scolding aides for taking too long to post. In the first few months of Hegseth’s tenure, she ordered Ullyot to turn a room just off the briefing room into a makeup studio.

“This was ridiculous. I said not only no, but hell no,” Ullyot writes. He warned that news of the makeup studio would leak. “How exactly did a makeup studio fit into the warrior ethos?”.

Industry observers note that in response to a detailed list of questions, Pentagon spokesman Joel Valdez declined to answer many of them but emailed a lengthy statement criticizing Ullyot. “There is no ‘makeup studio’ in the Pentagon, and it never existed,” Valdez stated, going on to call Ullyot “a skinwalker,” a “sour puss coward,” and “generally a stupid person” who left “his job in disgrace.” (According to information reviewed by Vanity Fair, Hegseth praised Ullyot after his departure from the Pentagon and offered to recommend him to Susie Wiles, then Trump’s chief of staff.).

“I volunteered to help stand up the Secretary’s press operation for a few months at the start of his term,” Ullyot told Vanity Fair in response. “I left as planned, and the Secretary thanked me for my work. My record over more than 30 years, including as a senior spokesman in the Senate and in the Trump White House, speaks for itself.”.

Sources indicate that hegseth was bullish on the war with Iran from the start. “There weren’t any real cheerleaders for the war in the cabinet outside of Pete Hegseth,” said the second official. “It was Pete and [US Ambassador to Israel] Mike Huckabee.”.

According to recent reports, soon after his confirmation, Hegseth moved to increase his powers and consolidate control over the Pentagon. He ousted generals and subjected senior staff to polygraph tests to weed out leakers, a crusade that resulted in the abrupt firings of top officials that demoralized staff. He tapped Tim Parlatore, his personal lawyer, as a special adviser and charged him with overseeing leak investigations. Parlatore continued to run his own private practice as a criminal defense attorney, and Politico reported this week that while serving as Hegseth’s top adviser, he is representing the son of a Libyan warlord accused of extrajudicial killings and torture.

Recent findings suggest that in keeping with the president’s broad campaign for retribution, Hegseth ordered an investigation into retired Joint Chiefs Chairman General Mark Milley, who had clashed with Trump during his first term, and stripped the four-star general of his security detail. The Pentagon is now working on a newly introduced report on the 2021 Kabul Airport attack, during which 13 American soldiers and 170 Afghan civilians were killed in a suicide bombing during the withdrawal from Afghanistan. At the time, Milley served as chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff. The new assessment, one source familiar with the investigation said, is expected by the end of the month and is intended to serve as a predicate to strip Milley of his four-star rank.

It has been revealed that hegseth waged a parallel war on the press, starting with an attempt to ban NBC News correspondent Courtney Kube from the Pentagon. In a meeting with his advisers, Ullyot writes, Hegseth explained that he and his wife Jennifer were “angry” at Kube for how much she covered his turbulent confirmation process before Congress. “I thought this was loony tunes,” Ullyot writes. One source told me that after NBC News was kicked out of its Pentagon office, Hegseth aides took a full-length mirror from the vacated room and installed it in his makeup studio.

In a recent development, as Hegseth purged senior officials, he grew closer to Buria. The relationship was confounding to many inside the building: Hegseth has pushed to cleanse the Pentagon of ideological diversity, yet he elevated Buria, a holdover from the Biden administration who had previously donated to Democrats. But Buria had earned the trust of Jennifer. When explaining to advisers why he was elevated, Hegseth remarked he prayed about the decision with his wife. “And you know what? Jen says he’s really good with the kids,” Hegseth told them.

In a recent development, buria was by Hegseth’s side throughout the Signalgate scandal, which, according to several administration officials, was a turning point for the secretary. “Every problem he is having in one way or another goes back to Signalgate,” the second Trump official stated. “His extremely hostile relations with the press, his paranoia, his firing of certain people, denied promotions to generals. It was all around paranoia related to Signalgate.”.

“There’s two versions of Hegseth,” said a second former defense official. “There is the pre-Signalgate version and the post-Signalgate version. It’s like Jekyll and Hyde. He was Dr. Jekyll until around Signalgate, and he’s been Mr. Hyde ever since. He’s just not making good decisions.”.

It was an almost unbelievable incident: Hegseth shared war prepares for a bombing campaign against the Houthis in Yemen on at least two Signal group chats, including one that inadvertently included Jeffrey Goldberg, the editor in chief of The Atlantic.

This was the first major military engagement of Hegseth’s tenure, but he chose to survey the operation with Buria from a temporary secure facility at his Fort McNair home rather than make the short trip to the Pentagon or the White House Situation Room. The decision alarmed some at the Pentagon. “It’s your first major military operation,” said the second senior Trump official. “Why would you monitor it from your shitty SCIF in your basement? Why not go 10 minutes to the Pentagon where you have the joint staff?”.

“You would think with kinetic operations going on in the Middle East that could have dramatic consequences for service members, that he’d be in the office,” Tillis said.

Trump has so far backed Hegseth publicly, and last week, House Republicans blocked the impeachment effort. “Pete is a fighter,” the White House official explained. “Trump likes fighters.”.

Industry observers note that during Hegseth’s confirmation process, allegations of heavy drinking concerned Republican lawmakers he needed to vote in favor of his nomination. At the time, several Republican senators said he promised them he would stop boozing if confirmed. He affirmed this pledge publicly: “This is the biggest deployment of my life,” he told Megyn Kelly in a 2024 interview, “and there won’t be a drop of alcohol on my lips while I’m doing it.”.

Whether or not Hegseth has actually quit drinking continues to be a source of palace intrigue. One official recalled watching Hegseth drink what the secretary suggested were two cocktails—though the official conceded he hadn’t seen the drinks poured, and raised a theory that Hegseth might have been testing whether he would leak the incident to the press. “This was at a time of peak paranoia,” the official stated.

In a recent development, buria was known to drink on official trips; the official recalled Hegseth’s aide handing out shots to passengers on a US government jet during a Pentagon junket. Two other officials said Buria would often brag about drinking with Hegseth, including on an official trip to Panama in 2025. The Fresh York Post later reported that Buria had made up a story about him and Hegseth donning disguises to go out and drink, all in an effort to weed out leakers. One of the officials told me they believed the leak claim was Buria’s retroactive effort to cover up that he was boasting about drinking with the secretary.

Recent findings suggest that “The drinking is what they’re really afraid of,” the second official noted. When asked directly if Hegseth continued drinking as secretary, a Defense Department spokesperson who declined to be named said in a statement: “No, the Secretary has kept his promise that he made during his confirmation hearings and has not drank since becoming Secretary of War.”.

According to recent reports, jennifer and Pete Hegseth have forged a close relationship with Stephen Miller and his wife Katie, their neighbors on a placid and heavily fortified army base south of the White House. Hegseth’s temporary salvation comes thanks in part to support from Miller, who values his deference to Trump. “Stephen doesn’t like all the Liberace shit, the cucaracha shit,” mentioned the first former official. “Pete right now is fresh out of friends, and misery loves tech giant. But don’t get it twisted. At any moment, at any second, Stephen will cut Pete’s throat.”.

In a recent development, the secretary of defense has made few friends in Washington. One source recalled attending a holiday party stocked with members of the administration during which Hegseth spent much of his time alone in the corner of the room. “Even Kash Patel had people coming up to him to talk,” the source mentioned. “Pete was alone and isolated. He looked depressed. And this was before the Iran war. His stock has not gone up since then.”.

In a recent development, hegseth has channeled much of his effort into appealing to an audience of one, telling advisers he only cares about Trump’s opinion. “The one thing he’s been successful at, and I think it’s the only thing, is flattering Donald Trump constantly,” the former official stated.

The purpose of this flattery campaign extends beyond keeping his current job. In private, Hegseth has confided in several officials about his ambitions to run for president. This jockeying has exacerbated tensions with Vice President JD Vance. The relationship was already strained by Vance’s private opposition to the Iran war, and it deteriorated significantly after the vice president’s close friend, Dan Driscoll, was pushed out of his position as Army Secretary in August following months of friction with Hegseth.

Industry observers note that when explaining to advisers why Buria was elevated, Hegseth mentioned he prayed about the decision with his wife. “And you know what? Jen notes he’s really good with the kids,” Hegseth told them.

“Secretary Hegseth and Vice President Vance share an outstanding working relationship grounded in deep mutual respect and alignment,” Parnell noted in a statement to Vanity Fair.

Recent findings suggest that jennifer has worked in tandem with her husband to push allies on social media and in the press to promote the idea of a presidential run. “She wants to be first lady,” the former official said of Jennifer. “She wants to be Hillary.” After the midterms, online influencers whom Hegseth hired earlier this year to work as special government employees at the Pentagon began pitching Hegseth for president. These influencers were nominally hired to promote Hegseth’s efforts to bring war colleges in line with the “warrior ethos,” but in reality they coordinated with Jennifer and Radabaugh on “shitposting,” the second official said. Earlier this month, they rallied to Hegseth’s defense as he came under fire for the Republican ballot box-bloodbath, posting action shots of the secretary with the caption: “STAND. FIGHT. DEFEND THE REPUBLIC.”.

According to recent reports, these influencers often attack journalists who cover the Pentagon. In response to a recent story by Politico’s Daniel Lippman, an active-duty Army officer known as InfantryDort on social media—whom Hegseth hired as one of these shadow spokespeople—posted: “I expect you all to ratio the fuck out of this retard and in short order. Daniel Lippman remains absolute journalistic filth.” A Politico spokesperson responded: “Daniel is one of Washington’s best-sourced reporters, and we’re lucky to have him at POLITICO.”.

In a recent development, when Democrats take control of Congress, they are expected to focus much of their oversight on Hegseth, including the scandals from his personal life. The subjects broached in his contentious confirmation hearings—including an affidavit signed by his former sister-in-law alleging abuse against his second wife—are likely to be relitigated. (His second wife denied that she was physically abused.).

Industry observers note that “Is that going to be good for the president?” Tillis asked. “His entire confirmation will be re-prosecuted. That affidavit will get a lot of attention. Family members will most likely be subpoenaed. Does he really want to go through that at a personal level, and at the same time be such a massive disruption for the leader of the most lethal, complex organization in American government? Is this about Pete, or is this about America’s defense? I don’t know how any objective person can say that the value that he brings is greater than that distraction and the cost of him remaining in place.”.

Industry observers note that “If he had any dignity, he would resign and allow the president to appoint a replacement in the lame duck session,” said the first official. “But he doesn’t.”.

Hegseth’s ability to project confidence is not confined to the cameras. He was bullish on the war with Iran from the start. “There weren’t any real cheerleaders for the war in the cabinet outside of Pete Hegseth,” said the second official. “It was Pete and [US Ambassador to Israel] Mike Huckabee.” In late December 2025, Hegseth met with Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu at the Four Seasons in Palm Beach shortly before Netanyahu ventured to Mar-a-Lago to make the case for fresh strikes on Iran. By February, Netanyahu was pushing Trump to join Israel in a full-blown war to topple the Iranian regime.

Hegseth was all-in, his confidence buoyed by the success of Operation Midnight Hammer—a series of strikes on Iranian nuclear facilities in June 2025—and the raid to abduct Venezuelan dictator Nicolás Maduro. His allies in the administration point to these operations, as well as a post-pandemic surge in military recruitment numbers, as his major successes in the job.

In a recent development, but multiple officials who spoke with Vanity Fair said they believed that when briefing Trump, Hegseth understated the risks of war with Iran from the beginning and went on to overstate its successes as the conflict dragged on. “Pete gave the rosiest picture in the world,” said the first former official. During early discussions about potentially launching the war, the official said they were struck by how promptly Hegseth started speaking about the operation as a “foregone conclusion.”.

“Leading up into the war, he presented, along with [Central Command Commander Admiral] Brad Cooper, overly optimistic projections of what the air campaign could achieve,” said the second administration official. “This is how the president got this idea that it could be done in a matter of two to three weeks.”.

Industry observers note that hegseth ran against Democrat U.S. Senator Amy Klobuchar in 2012.

Sources indicate that tillis, for his part, said that he did not believe Hegseth was forthright with Trump about the war. “He planned the good, bright, shiny stuff that was Epic Fury, but clearly did not brief the president on things that anybody that’s had any experience in the Middle East knows,” Tillis added. “The first thing that goes is the Strait of Hormuz.”.

“Secretary Hegseth and Pentagon leadership consistently provide the President with the complete, unvarnished picture so he can make the best choices for America’s security and success,” Parnell remarked in a statement.

On the first day of the war, a missile struck the Minab elementary school in southern Iran, killing more than 150 people, the majority of them children. The US military has thus far refused to publicly admit responsibility for the strike, despite a preliminary military investigation concluding within days of the strike that a US missile struck the school. Before the attack, Hegseth gutted the Pentagon program aimed at reducing civilian harm during military operations, ProPublica reported in March. House Republican Thomas Massie, who brought the articles of impeachment against Hegseth last week, argued the bombing was “the result of systemic deterioration and removal of Department of Defense infrastructure that Congress had mandated by law to limit collateral damage to civilians.”.

Massie cast the strike as a consequence of Hegseth’s oft-repeated mantra: “Maximum lethality, not tepid legality.”.

As the war went on, officials said, Hegseth continued to trumpet its successes, showing the president what one official described as “hype videos” depicting strikes on missile launchers, Iranian ships, and old aircraft. Hegseth told Trump “that the majority of Iran’s missile capabilities and the majority of Iran’s Air Force was destroyed,” the official said, even though US intelligence “showed that wasn’t the case, and that the majority of Iran’s missiles and missile launchers by the end of the major combat phase of the war were still intact.”.

“He creates an echo chamber in the press corps so that he can get only nice questions or do made-for-TV stuff,” noted Senator Tillis.

According to recent reports, hegseth also worked behind the scenes to promote positive media coverage of the war. He briefed Fox News hosts whom he remained friendly with on the war’s progress and encouraged them to present a positive picture on air. But Hegseth himself has made little effort to explain or defend the war to Americans. Even as the war has become a political debacle for the administration, he remains bullish on escalation. “Pete is the only one who wants to restart strikes,” the first official mentioned.

According to recent reports, we were all sitting in our assigned seats waiting for the performance to start when a security official walked into the Pentagon briefing room to make an announcement. Hegseth had not held a Pentagon press briefing since May. Now, facing an impeachment effort from a member of his own party, he came before the cameras. “If anyone gets out of line today, you’re going to be physically removed,” the official remarked. “Is that clear?”.

According to recent reports, “Sense of decorum,” the official noted apologetically. “Just be professional.”.

The official said he was just relaying orders from Hegseth’s office. A few minutes later, Joel Valdez, the press aide, walked out and asked if anyone was confused. Everyone was. “I could tell you off the record?” he said. No, the reporters replied. “Do you want to hear it off the record?” No, they said again.

Industry observers note that valdez looked down at his shoes and then walked out of the room without saying another word. “In my 30 years in DC, I have never heard that,” remarked a cameraman. “This is crazytown.”.

At 8 a.m. sharp, Hegseth walked out wearing a loud plaid suit, a striped tie, and an American flag pocket square. The timing is no coincidence; officials said Hegseth schedules briefings in the 8 a.m. hour because Trump is known to watch Fox News at that time.

According to recent reports, the secretary of defense began reading his speech from a stack of papers on the podium. From my assigned seat in the back row, I felt as if I were watching an interpretive dance. The choreography of Hegseth’s hand movements and facial expressions was as slick as his hair, which was gelled into a stiff meringue that moved in unison with his tanned face.

Industry observers note that hegseth punctuated a line about President Trump’s “decisive” leadership with a clenched fist thrust downward. The word “overseeing” was expressed with a slow swipe of the hand over an imaginary stretch of purview. As Hegseth recalled the glories of the Maduro operation—and, parenthetically, his part in directing them—he dismissed criticism of the raid by leaning into the microphone, shaking his head from side to side and wiggling his eyebrows: “It wasn’t”—dramatic pause for eyebrow wiggle—“a kidnapping.”.

Hegseth's presser had a pantomime quality.

In a recent development, the briefing itself exuded little of the confidence Hegseth sought to signal before the cameras. He took seven questions in total, sticking to friendly reporters in the front rows who had signed a pledge in September 2025 to not report “unauthorized information” from the Pentagon. One of them, a representative of Real America’s Voice, asked “what message” is sent to America’s allies when “our own politicians don’t support taking out the narco traffickers that kill their own constituents?” It wasn’t so much a question as a warm bath. Some in the room, visibly frustrated by the waste of time, rolled their eyes. Others shouted questions from the back about Iran and impeachment. Hegseth refused to look at them.

“He creates an echo chamber in the press corps so that he can get only nice questions or do made-for-TV stuff,” said Tillis, who also decried Hegseth for filming a slick video of himself outside the Department of Defense making the case for why he should not be impeached: “He demonstrated more impulsiveness by using taxpayer dollars to defend himself against impeachment.”.

It has been revealed that in his remarks before the press, Hegseth framed the effort to remove him as an attack on the troops. “If they want to come for the warriors, they’re going to have to come through me,” he said, jabbing a finger into his chest. But the impeachment targeted Hegseth, not “the warriors.” We had assembled to hear Pete make the case for Pete. Indeed, he had not held a press briefing when a Navy commander died in a helicopter crash on July 1, or when three US soldiers were killed in an Iranian strike on a base in Jordan on July 17. What brought him back before the cameras was not the ongoing war in the Middle East but his own fight to save his career here in Washington.

According to recent reports, the performance earned a rave review from the one viewer who mattered. “Pete Hegseth gets an ‘A’ PLUS, PLUS, PLUS,” Trump wrote on Truth Social.

According to recent reports, early on in Hegseth’s tenure, he confided in advisers about his “biggest fear” as he took on the mighty responsibility of leading the Department of Defense, the first former official told me: “Being fired and embarrassed.” For now, Trump is standing by his secretary. He always is, until he isn’t. When asked just before the midterms whether Wiles would remain on as his chief of staff, Trump said there was “zero chance” he’d replace her. Three weeks later, she was out.

The Pokemon franchise turned 30 this year, and while you'll have to wait until next year for a newly introduced mainline game installment, you can celebrate that anniversary with something that's much cooler: Rock-and-roll-type electric guitars. The Pokemon Manufacturer revealed that it teamed up with guitar manufacturer Fender to produce a Stratocaster model inspired by Pokemon Red, and a Telecaster model inspired by Pokemon Green. Each guitar features an aesthetic that pays tribute to the original Pokemon Game Boy adventures, including pixel art pulled from the games, graphics, and color overlays for an extra pop. The guitars really shine with a special toggle that warps the music they produce into an 8-bit retro sound that’s reminiscent of vintage gaming hardware. The neck also pays homage to Pokemon, with a special design that commemorates the collaboration between Fender and Pokemon. Just remember: No Stairway. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tDt6S_MIk8A As you'd expect, these won't be cheap. While US pricing and availability will be confirmed later on the Pokemon Center retail site, in Japan, these will retail for around $2,600 each. You'll also need to enter a lottery to stand a chance at winning the option to purchase one of these Fenders, which should prevent the items from being pounced on en masse by Pokemon scalpers. This year has seen several promotions kick off to celebrate 30 years of Pokemon, and one of the biggest involved Krispy Kreme. The doughnut chain's boxes of digestible pocket monsters proved highly popular, and unsurprisingly, Pokemon scalpers wasted no time trying to flip those treats and packaging for cash online. At least the legally distinct Pokemoan sex toys re-released this year proved to be somewhat immune to scalper efforts.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Update, 8:41 p.m.: The Federal Aviation Administration unveiled it has ended the ground stop.
  • On Friday afternoon, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ordered a nationwide ground stop for all airports in the United States.
  • Recent findings suggest that there are a number of options for tracking flights, whether you have your flight number or not.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Update, 8:41 p.m.: The Federal Aviation Administration unveiled it has ended the ground stop.

On Friday afternoon, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ordered a nationwide ground stop for all airports in the United States. If you're planning to fly this afternoon or evening, or you have friends or family doing the same, you're likely concerned about tracking flight statuses. While there's still a lot we don't know, there are tools to help track flights at this time:.

Recent findings suggest that there are a number of options for tracking flights, whether you have your flight number or not. If you have the flight number, the fastest method is to Google it: Google will display a live tracker of your flight at the top of the results page. You can also head to the airline's official website to track your flight: United Airlines, for example, has a flight tracker where you can either enter your route information or your flight number. Most, if not all, airlines will have a similar tool you can use.

In a recent development, alternatively, you can use a site or service that tracks all flights. FlightAware is one such site and has a flight tracker that lets you search flights—so long as you know the origin and the destination. If you have the flight number, your iPhone can help: You can enter your flight number into Spotlight search to see a live tracker, or you can text a contact your flight number, then tap the link that appears under the number to see a tracker of the flight.

At this time, the exact reason isn't totally clear. According to the agency, “The FAA issued a nationwide ground stop for all U.S. airports following communication challenges impacting multiple Air Route Traffic Control Centers,” but the FAA hasn't said what caused those communications issues or when they expect to lift the grounding. The grounding order comes one day after a massive Microsoft outage that disrupted service for users of Outlook, Teams, and other Microsoft products. It also comes one day after Ars Technica reported that the FAA was rolling out an AI-powered tool to help manage air traffic across the country.

This is only the third time in U.S. history that the FAA has made such an order—once after 9/11, and again in January of 2023 due to a pilot alert system issue; the latter ground stop lasted around 90 minutes.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Grand Theft Auto 6 is somehow off to an even hotter start than many expected.
  • Sources indicate that many users across Reddit, X, and other platforms have reported this problem, which has an error code of CE-108255-1.
  • Recent findings suggest that others reported the same problem, with some able to work around it by changing their PS5’s resolution from Manual to 1080p in the system settings.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 is somehow off to an even hotter start than many expected. The game sold 32.5 million copies pre-release, bringing in a whopping $3.79 billion on day one. That makes it the biggest entertainment launch in history, according to publisher Take-Two. Unfortunately, though, not everyone has been able to enjoy the fun. Numerous players have reported that they can't progress in the game due to a persistent PlayStation 5 crashthat sends them back to the dashboard.

Sources indicate that many users across Reddit, X, and other platforms have reported this problem, which has an error code of CE-108255-1. The crash happens under a range of circumstances. Some are seeing the error in the prologue, while others don't encounter it until hours in; it can appear at a consistent point or at random. One Redditor wrote that they get the error whenever Jason is about to use a plunger in the Pipework mission, keeping them trapped in purgatory with Mandy. This Redditor said they spoke with Rockstar Games’ customer support about the issue and were told to contact PlayStation’s hardware support team, implying that Rockstar believes this is a PS5 hardware problem.

Recent findings suggest that others reported the same problem, with some able to work around it by changing their PS5’s resolution from Manual to 1080p in the system settings. Other popular “fixes” include clearing the PS5’s cache, rebuilding the database, reinstalling the game, updating the system’s firmware, or restoring the PS5 license. It seems these solutions are working for some but not for others. In some cases, people mentioned that they had encountered the problem before with other games.

According to Sony’s support page, the CE-108255-1 error is a generic code for “An error occurred with the game/application,” and Sony suggests that those who receive the error revision their game or visit the company’s PlayStation Repairs page.

According to recent reports, there are competing theories about why the CE-108255-1 crash seems to be happening to so many GTA 6 players. One prevailing hypothesis is that it is a hardware problem. X user ghost_motley suggested that GTA 6 is so graphically intensive that it’s exposing existing complications with many consumers' PS5s. “This is great news for console repair technicians, who will have a new game to stress test consoles with,” they wrote. Rockstar has touted GTA 6’s detailed environments and ray tracing, saying the game won’t get a 60 fps performance mode on console because it is too graphically demanding. Some have theorized that GTA 6 may be exposing problems with the PS5’s “liquid metal” cooling solution: in some cases, the liquid metal has dried out over time, preventing the console from cooling properly.

It has been revealed that that noted, Gizmodo reported that PlayStation support told at least one person that the problem is a software problem, implying Rockstar is at fault. An X user claimed they went to the trouble of replacing their console’s liquid metal and still ran into the crash. While it seems that Rockstar and Sony's support teams are both at the moment suggesting the other party is to blame, hopefully both are quietly looking into a fix so more people can form their own opinions on the best-reviewed game of all time.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is available now on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X.

  • Rockstar Games just released Grand Theft Auto 6 on November 19 to rave reviews and huge sales.
  • Recent findings suggest that appearing on OpenAI's technology and business show TBPN recently, Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick was asked how a upcoming GTA game could possibly up the ante.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that rockstar Games just rolled out Grand Theft Auto 6 on November 19 to rave reviews and huge sales. Everyone wants to know what's coming next, and surely there will eventually be another GTA game, but not soon. Appearing on OpenAI's technology and business show TBPN recently, Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick was asked how a new GTA game could possibly up the ante. TBPN's Jordi Hays theorized that GTA 7 could "be a live version of the entire world." Zelnick, for his part, said people should remember that the interview was recorded on November 19, the day that GTA 6 released, so it's not time to talk about GTA 7. "I can't help myself. We at Take-Two just went live GTA 6 on November 19. Let me check my watch. Oh, it's still November 19. And you're asking a question about GTA 7," he said. While Rockstar isn't talking about GTA 7 yet--and no one should expect that to happen anytime soon--Take-Two has already signaled that the next GTA game could come out sooner. He said the “nature and velocity” of the company’s content releases in its major franchises, including GTA, will look “dramatically different over the next decade.” GTA 6 released more than 13 years after GTA 5 came out in 2013. However, development didn't begin in earnest on GTA 6 until after Red Dead Redemption II came out in 2018, according to reporter Jason Schreier. This is because Rockstar's network of studios around the world work together on one project at a time, though smaller teams are also cooking up new things simultaneously. For more, check out GameSpot's GTA 6 review and our rundown of the five best things to do first.

Sources indicate that good afternoon from Washington, where Party Animals has not forgotten the 5 a.m. wake-up required last Tuesday to attend Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth’s first Pentagon press conference in six months. This was a peculiar one, arranged so Hegseth could brief the public on his own personal battle for career survival.

In a recent development, the briefing kicked off at 8 a.m., but the press had to be at the Pentagon by 6 a.m. for an extensive security screening. I’d like to think that this cruel early start was a consequence of Hegseth’s self-proclaimed sobriety. What kind of drunk drags his sorry carcass before a crowd of jackals before noon? Not any I know.

It has been revealed that but sources I spoke with for a new piece on Hegseth’s war inside the Pentagon told me there was a more Machiavellian motivation for the presser: Donald Trump loves to watch Fox & Friends at 8 a.m. And sure enough, soon after the conclusion of Hegseth’s performance, its intended audience of one offered a review on Truth Social.

Read on for my investigation into Hegseth’s turbulent tenure at the top of the Department of Defense, and what it means for his survival as Democrats take control of Congress in January.

The reviews are in for Joe Biden’s upcoming book, Promise Me, America. The Atlantic calls the book “unrepentant.” The New York Times calls it a 400-page “cover letter.” The former president offers the fantastical opinion that he should have stayed in the race in 2024 and faced Trump, quite a position to maintain given he couldn’t voice his own audiobook and limited his press appearances for the release to a soft-focus People magazine story (his publisher did not respond to Party Animals’ multiple requests for an interview). According to the reviews, the former president dedicates scant attention to one of the biggest debacles of his presidency, the war in Gaza, which he abetted thanks to near-unwavering support for Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu as 2,000-pound bombs rained down on the densely packed enclave, killing more than 70,000 people. As president, Biden publicly questioned the death toll numbers. “Too many innocent Palestinians were killed,” he now writes, as if possessed by the passive-voice ghost of Donald Rumsfeld. Mistakes were made, indeed. In contrast with his remarkably clinical view of dead Gazans, he writes movingly about his friendship with Netanyahu, recalling his farewell to the prime minister days before leaving the White House: “I still love you, pal.”.

Elon Musk is Sorry About All That.

Just five months ago, Elon Musk was promoting a movie in which a gunman goes on a mass murder rampage targeting supporters of immigration. That this was barely noticed is a sign of just how extreme Musk’s rhetoric has become over the years, as he devolved Xeet by Xeet into the online equivalent of a bum who yells at strangers on the street about race science. Then the midterms happened. After blowing nearly $500 million in an effort to get Republicans elected and falling short in key races, particularly in Texas, the octocentibillionaire seems to be seeking some kind of public rehabilitation. In a virtual appearance at The Newly introduced York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday, Musk told Andrew Ross Sorkin that he is “not MAGA”—despite the many photos of Elon wearing a certain conspicuous hat—and that he is actually “a moderate.” Don’t take the hat’s word for it, though, here’s Musk on the record in October 2024: “I’m not just MAGA, I’m Dark MAGA.” Ah, well, nevertheless. He expressed hope for incoming Texas governor Gina Hinojosa, a Democrat, and noted he felt “foolish” for blowing so many millions to achieve very little. What’s the over/under on how long Moderate Elon will last?

According to recent reports, french, Toast: No one should know who “Bo” French is. Google Killed Its Dark Web Report, but You Can Still Monitor Data Breaches

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, google’s Dark Web Report used to be the only consumer-focused platform that let users scan major data breaches, dark web marketplaces, and private forums to see if their personal information had ended up in the hands of hackers.
  • Google indicates it sunsetted Dark Web Report because, although the information it provided was generally useful, the service failed to provide “helpful next steps” for customers whose data was found on the dark web.
  • Dark Web Report may not have been perfect, but it was the only early warning system of its kind that was available for personal use and let users run scans free of cost.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, google’s Dark Web Report used to be the only consumer-focused platform that let users scan major data breaches, dark web marketplaces, and private forums to see if their personal information had ended up in the hands of hackers. But the tech giant discontinued the service at the start of 2026, with new scans stopping on Jan. 15 and all accounts deleted on Feb. 16.

Google indicates it sunsetted Dark Web Report because, although the information it provided was generally useful, the service failed to provide “helpful next steps” for customers whose data was found on the dark web. Google promised a new service that would provide more actionable intel, but that service has yet to materialize, and there haven’t been any further announcements about it yet.

Dark Web Report may not have been perfect, but it was the only early warning system of its kind that was available for personal use and let users run scans free of cost. Now that it’s gone, however, there are plenty of other services that offer the same service at varying costs and levels of effectiveness. Let’s talk through the nature of the insight that Google's reports offered, how it collected that information in the first place, and what options exist in the market to replace it.

Google rolled out the Dark Web Report in March 2023 as a premium feature available to Google One customers, but later extended it for free to anyone with a Google account and moved it to the "Results about you" dashboard.

Sources indicate that you'd set up a monitoring profile with your name, date of birth, physical address, phone number, emails, and Social Security Number if you lived in the U.S. After that, you could head to the dashboard anytime you wanted to run a free scan across dark web forums and marketplaces, publicly disclosed corporate data breaches, and other hidden online spaces to see if any of your personal information had shown up there. It was easy to use—but not a lot of people knew it existed in the first place.

Sources indicate that it’s unclear what prompted the internal decision at Google, but in the absence of concrete next steps, it is reasonable to think the reports could create panic for the uninitiated. There’s no way to remove your information from the dark web once it’s already in circulation there. Still, having an early warning so you could reset 2FA or self-lock your SSN isn’t without merit.

It has been revealed that but perhaps more importantly, most people with Google accounts didn’t know and hadn’t heard of the Dark Web Report’s existence. Google has likely taken it as a hint that users want more active remediation tools than simple alerts, which is why it’s now directing users to the Password Manager, Passkeys, and “Results about you” dashboard instead—though, again, the manufacturer hasn't followed through on a direct replacement for Dark Web Report, despite teasing such a feature.

Many of the top dark web scanners draw from the same well of information, scanning against major data breaches and dark web spaces. Several also offer breach notifications that send you email alerts when your details show up in a periodic scan. However, none of that is worth paying for because Have I Been Pwned or Mozilla Monitor cover those features quite well for free. Even the default password managers from Google and Apple come with some ability to monitor leaked credentials.

According to recent reports, there isn’t an easy way to scrub your information from the dark web once it ends up getting leaked. But you can take steps to protect sensitive information or financial data once you know there’s been a leak. If a password has been compromised, reset it immediately. Also, enable 2FA on the affected account for added security. Even better, switch to a passkey if that account supports it. If not, authenticator apps are a safer way to receive 2FA codes than standard SMS.

According to recent reports, if your Social Security number has been leaked, freeze your credit with Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion. You can do this by contacting each agency separately. Freezing your credit will prevent unauthorized credit withdrawals and protect your credit score from abuse by attackers. If one of your credit or debit card numbers has ended up in a breach, call your bank to freeze transactions on that card immediately.

Finally, get in the habit of using email aliases instead of sharing your actual email address with every platform and service provider. Addy.io and Proton’s SimpleLogin are both popular services that let you generate temporary email aliases that point to your inbox.

Taylor called the experience “eye-opening” and urged fans not to take their health for granted. “I did for many years and I won’t ever do that again,” he mentioned. “Next week on November 28 will mark my 2 year sobriety anniversary and I’m so fucking proud. It’s crazy how things happen…if I hadn’t ended up in the hospital with that kidney stone, I probably wouldn’t have known this tumor was there until it was too late.” He concluded, “I like to think my dad had a part in that. Life can really change in a second. I’ve been given a lot to think about these past few years and if there’s one thing I know for sure it’s that nothing else matters more than your health your kids and the people that show up for you when it matters the most.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that GTA 6 is an enormous hit--it's the biggest gaming release ever. Take-Two just announced that GTA 6 reach 32.5 million copies sold before release, with revenue reaching $3.79 billion through the end of the first day on sale on November 19. This makes it the biggest entertainment release--for any medium--in history, Take-Two said. For comparison, 2013's GTA 5 hit $800 million in revenue in its first 24 hours and $1 billion after its first three days, so GTA 6 is pacing well ahead of those numbers. GTA 5 launched at $60, compared to $80 for the cheapest version of GTA 6. For comparison, the all-time highest-grossing movie ever is Avengers: Endgame, which made $2.94 billion during its entire run. GTA 6 has done nearly $1 billion more in revenue already. According to reporter Jason Schreier, GTA 6 is also now instantly one of the top 30 best-selling games of all time. “It is with immense gratitude that we enter a latest chapter of Rockstar Gameswith the release of Grand Theft Auto VI,” Rockstar president and co-founder Sam Houser said. “We are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world and we couldn’t be more excited to share this moment with you.” https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1YEHOKYVTho Massive numbers for GTA 6 were always expected. Sensor Tower had been sharing unofficial sales data for GTA 6 for a long time already, but Take-Two's sales numbers are even higher than the 25 million sales that Sensor Tower reported at launch. GTA 6 is only going to get bigger when it comes to sales as more and more people buy the game. Additionally, GTA 6 is expected to come to PC in 2027, which will be another selling cycle for the game. Beyond this, GTA 6 is expected to add an online mode in 2027 that will no doubt feature microtransactions and other ways for Rockstar to make money off the fanbase. For more, check out GameSpot’s GTA 6 review and our rundown of the five best things to do first. And if you’re eager for news on GTA 7? Get comfortable, because Rockstar is not going to announce it anytime soon.
